costGuide.title: Mercedes-AMG M156 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an M156 engine typically takes 14-18 hours at £75-£95/hr (AMG specialist) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this engine is the condition of the camshaft adjusters (phasers), hydraulic lifters, and oil cooler seals. Because the M156 is a high-performance, hand-built AMG unit, reputable recon specialists will typically replace all eight camshaft adjusters, inspect and replace any collapsed lifters, and renew all brittle valve cover and oil seals as standard to prevent immediate post-installation failures. failures.title: Mercedes-AMG M156 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Camshaft Adjuster (Phaser) Failure
items.whatHappens: The M156 uses variable valve timing via camshaft adjusters on all four camshafts. The internal vanes or seals within these adjusters can wear or fail, causing a loud rattling noise on cold startup, check engine lights (camshaft position correlation codes), and rough idling.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the camshaft adjusters is a known, albeit labour-intensive, repair (requiring removal of the valve covers and timing components). If ignored, it can lead to timing jumps and catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

items.title: Hydraulic Lifter Tick and Collapse
items.whatHappens: The hydraulic valve lifters can wear, collapse, or become clogged with sludge if oil change intervals were extended. This manifests as a distinct ticking or tapping noise from the top of the engine, particularly noticeable at idle or under load.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the affected lifters and ensuring pristine oil quality can resolve the issue. If a collapsed lifter has caused excessive camshaft wear, a full cylinder head rebuild or reconditioned engine is required.

items.title: Oil Cooler Seal Leaks
items.whatHappens: The oil cooler, located at the front of the engine, relies on rubber seals that harden and shrink over time due to heat cycles. This leads to external oil leaks, which can drip onto the subframe or exhaust components, creating a burning smell and potential fire risk.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a routine maintenance item. Replacing the oil cooler seals is relatively inexpensive in terms of parts, though it requires careful access around the front ancillary components.

failures.goodYearsLine: The M156 is widely regarded as one of the greatest naturally aspirated V8 engines ever built. Units maintained with strict, frequent oil changes (every 5,000-7,000 miles) and timely camshaft adjuster replacements routinely exceed 150,000 miles without major internal bottom-end issues .

variants.title: M156 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: The M156 family shares the same fundamental 6.2L DOHC V8 block architecture, but power output, intake manifolds, and engine management vary significantly depending on the chassis. Identifying your exact sub-code is mandatory, as fitting the wrong revision can lead to severe mechanical and ECU incompatibility. - Fitted to: S-Class W221 (S 63 AMG), CL-Class W216 (CL 63 AMG), E-Class W212 (early E 63 AMG) - Key technical difference: The flagship high-output variant, featuring a revised intake manifold, specific AMG engine management calibration, and (in the S/CL-Class) a higher output tune of 544 hp compared to the standard 525 hp found in early E-Class applications. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; the higher continuous thermal loads in the heavy S/CL-Class chassis can accelerate oil cooler seal degradation. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with the C 63 AMG (.985) variant due to different engine mounts, wiring harnesses, intake plumbing, and ECU mapping. - Fitted to: M-Class W164 (ML 63 AMG), R-Class W251 (R 63 AMG) - Key technical difference: A slightly detuned variant optimized for SUV and MPV applications, featuring revised accessory brackets, heavy-duty engine mounts, and specific cooling system routing for off-road or high-payload use. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; SUV applications may experience accelerated oil cooler seal wear due to extreme operating angles and higher under-hood temperatures. - Interchange note: Requires matching sump, oil pickup, and accessory drives; passenger car variants are not directly interchangeable with SUV specs without significant modification. - Fitted to: C-Class W204 (C 63 AMG) - Key technical difference: The compact saloon/coupe variant, featuring a unique intake manifold, specific engine mounts for the W204 chassis, and a distinct wiring harness layout. Later models (2012+) featured the "AMG Performance Package" with 358 kW (487 hp). - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; highly susceptible to camshaft adjuster wear due to the compact engine bay and intense heat soak. - Interchange note: Not interchangeable with the .980 without swapping the intake manifold, engine mounts, wiring harness, and ECU.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement M156 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used M156 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable, stamped service history and documented proof of recent camshaft adjuster replacement and lifter inspection. Given the high-performance nature of these vehicles, buying a used unit with unknown history is a significant financial risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned M156 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by replacing all eight camshaft adjusters, inspecting and replacing any worn hydraulic lifters, and renewing all brittle valve cover and oil cooler seals, giving the engine a fresh, reliable lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full M156 engine rebuild is highly justified for low-mileage or collector W221 S 63 AMG or W216 CL 63 AMG restorations where originality, matching numbers (and the builder's signature plaque), and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your M156 engine is installed by specialists familiar with hand-built AMG V8 systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the M156 is typically found in W221, W216, W212, and W164 vehicles valued between £8,000 and £30,000+ (with low-mileage examples commanding significantly higher premiums), a full replacement is generally financially viable and protects the asset's value. However, if the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate the investment carefully .

items.question: How much does a Mercedes M156 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes-AMG M156 engine typically costs between £4,500 and £7,000 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £5,500 to £8,500 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £1,500 but carry a high financial risk due to the potential for camshaft adjuster and lifter wear. items.question: What is the most common failure on the M156 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are camshaft adjuster (phaser) failure, hydraulic lifter tick or collapse, and oil cooler seal leaks. The camshaft adjusters can cause a loud cold-start rattle and timing correlation codes, while collapsed lifters often result from extended oil change intervals leading to sludge buildup.
